gaps.missing: TWO defects in one label. (1) `overrides` is in the javascript comparison set and the oracle derives no `overrides` truth at all, so every analyzer override edge is unmatched — the same shape as the `imports` and `extends` gaps, and the third instance in this lane. (2) The edges are largely unfounded: the analyzer matches method NAMES across a class boundary to a base it cannot resolve, and emits `overrides` for names that cannot be members of that base.
gaps.evidence:
**HOW (1) WAS FOUND, which is the reusable part.** A gated per-label truth dump (BB_LABEL_DUMP) prints, per label, how many TRUTH rows the oracle derived and how many ANALYZER rows were comparable. A label with `truth=0` and `comparable>0` is being compared against nothing. That check found `extends` first — fixed in the same session, 8 truth rows added, unexplained 2 -> 0 at a 400-file sample — and then `overrides`. Without it `overrides` is invisible: its edges sit at 0.5, so the harness files them as `heuristic`, and a bucket full of suspicion reads as caution rather than as a hole. That is why X9 could be closed honestly as 'true edges the truth cannot adjudicate' and why that closure was still incomplete: the bucket also held edges that are simply wrong. **THE FULL-CORPUS POPULATION, 3,369 files: 50 override edges naming a qualified base, across 7 builtin bases.** They are not equivalent rows. TRUE members (the base really has them): `URLSearchParams.*` — append, delete, entries, forEach, get, getAll, has, keys, set, sort, toString, values, [Symbol.iterator]; `Map.*` — clear, delete, entries, forEach, get, has, keys, set, values, [Symbol.iterator]; `Set.*` — add, clear, delete, entries, forEach, has, keys, values. **CANNOT BE MEMBERS — the defects.** (a) PRIVATE AND IMPLEMENTATION NAMES, 8 of 50: `URLSearchParams.#update_url`, `URLSearchParams.[REPLACE]`, `Map.#read_all`, `Map.#source`, `Set.#init`, `Set.#source`, `Date.#init`, `HTMLElement.$$g_p`. A `#name` is a private field, scoped to the class body and NOT a prototype member, so it cannot override anything on a base; `[REPLACE]` is a template marker and `$$g_p` is a Svelte-internal field. (b) CUSTOM-ELEMENT CALLBACKS, 3 of 50: `HTMLElement.connectedCallback`, `.disconnectedCallback`, `.attributeChangedCallback` — hooks the browser INVOKES on a custom element, not members of HTMLElement, so nothing is overridden. (c) INHERITED, NOT OWN, 2 of 50: `HTMLElement.addEventListener` / `.removeEventListener` live on `EventTarget.prototype`. (d) NON-STANDARD, 2 of 50: `Error.toJSON`, `URL.toJSON`. So the analyzer's guess is right about 39 of 50 and wrong about 11. **THE MECHANISM IS NAMED BY THE ANALYZER ITSELF**: every one carries `reasonCode: "first-parent-guess"` and `evidenceClass: "inferred"` at confidence 0.5. The analyzer is not asserting these, it is guessing. **WHY 0.5 IS NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the judgement.** The tier does real work — it is why these are suspicion rather than fabrication. But X9's closure said the oracle cannot adjudicate them because no corpus contains `URL`; that was correct, and it is also why this is a defect rather than a boundary. An edge that cannot be adjudicated AND cannot be true is not a declared uncertainty, it is a wrong answer wearing one. The private-field and custom-element-callback rows are DECIDABLE — a `#name` is never a prototype member — so they are not in the heuristic bucket's intended population at all. **PART 1, LANDED.** The `#private` half is fixed: a `#name` is class-scoped, installed on each instance at construction and never on the prototype, so it can neither be declared by a base nor shadowed by a subclass. The guard is one line in the pass-3 branch and nothing else about it changed. Measured over the full corpus: 50 override edges over 7 bases becomes 44 over 6, with the private count zero on every base — and `Date` disappears entirely, because its only override edge in the whole corpus was `#init`. A/B on the tree: 44 with the guard, 50 without. The fixture pins BOTH directions, and that matters more than the guard itself — a blanket suppression of pass 3 also removes ~35 rows that are very likely true, and the edge COUNT is identical either way, so only naming the right rows catches a fix that is too broad. The fixture also covers a private METHOD, so the rule is not accidentally a field-shape test.
 **PART 2, AND THE PER-BASE SPLIT IS THE USEFUL PART.** The remaining 44 rows are NOT uniformly suspicious; the false rate is base-dependent and the corpus shows it plainly:
  `Map.*` 10 rows, 9 of which are real Map members; `Set.*` 8 rows, 7 real; `URLSearchParams.*` 14 rows, 12 real. Against that: **`HTMLElement.*` is 6 rows and ALL SIX ARE FALSE.** `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` live on `EventTarget.prototype`, and `connectedCallback` / `disconnectedCallback` / `attributeChangedCallback` are custom-element hooks the browser INVOKES — none is a member of `HTMLElement`.
  The sixth is `$$g_p`, and it is worth being precise about WHY it is false, because the obvious reading is wrong: `$$g_p(attribute_name) { … }` at line 216 is shorthand METHOD syntax and is classified `method` correctly, so this is not a field-vs-method misclassification. The reason is that `SvelteElement` ADDS methods rather than overriding them — which is exactly what a custom element is for. A name-based guess cannot tell adding from overriding, and that is the whole failure mode.
  So the honest summary is not "some of these are wrong". It is: against a base whose members the subclass genuinely shadows, the guess is right about 80-90%; against a base it merely EXTENDS, it is right about 0%. Neither rate is knowable from the corpus, because the discriminator is whether the name is a member of the builtin — and no corpus contains `HTMLElement`'s prototype. **WHAT BUILDING IT COST, since three of my own errors are the interesting part.** (1) The oracle refused ALL 44 rows including `Map.get`, because the class's members live under `class_body` and the first cut iterated the class node's own children — the same grandchild mistake the CSS import oracle records, and it failed the same way. (2) It then produced 12 MISSING because it skipped only fields whose INITIALISER was a literal, while `SvelteURL extends URL` re-declares `hash`, `host`, `href` and nine more as fields initialised with EXPRESSIONS — the property is a property regardless of what initialises it, so filtering on the initialiser was filtering on the wrong thing. All fields are now skipped. (3) It produced 12 MORE MISSING because it read accessors as methods, while the analyzer classifies an accessor as `property` and scopes `overrides` to Methods and Constructors — see J10. Each error was found by reading the MISSING rows rather than by reasoning about them, which is the only reason they were found at all: a partial oracle that is simply wrong produces MISSING, and MISSING names the file and the line.
gaps.status: CLOSED — both parts landed. `overrides` now has a truth oracle, and every override edge the analyzer emits is a confirmed member of the base it names (was 84%).
gaps.closure:
BOTH PARTS CLOSED, and part 2 was decided by measurement rather than by argument.
**PART 1** — the `#private` rule: a `#name` is class-scoped, installed on each instance and never on the prototype, so it can neither be declared by a base nor shadowed by a subclass. Implemented as one line in the pass-3 branch, measured 50 -> 44 edges and 7 bases -> 6, A/B-proven, with a fixture that fails both on reverting the guard and on deleting the branch.
**PART 2** — the unresolvable-base design question, settled by building the thing the question was about: `src/ast/js-builtin-prototypes.ts`, one declaration of the platform prototype CHAINS and their members, imported by BOTH the analyzer and the oracle. Two copies could drift apart unnoticed, which is the shared-premise shape this investigation kept meeting, so there is one.
  With the oracle in place the analyzer's guess could finally be MEASURED: of the 44 rows, 37 named a real member of the base and 7 did not. That ratio is what decided the question. Suppressing the whole first-parent guess would have deleted 37 CORRECT rows to remove 7 wrong ones, so the guess stays; the analyzer now consults the table and refuses only the provably-absent names. The decision rests on a count, not on how suspicious 0.5 feels — and it was only available because the oracle was built FIRST.
  The seven removed: `Error.toJSON` (not a standard Error member), the three custom-element callbacks `connectedCallback` / `disconnectedCallback` / `attributeChangedCallback` (hooks the browser INVOKES, not members of `HTMLElement`), `$$g_p` (a class field), and `[REPLACE]` (a template marker that merely looks like a computed key). `URL.toJSON` was KEPT and is correct — the WHATWG URL spec defines it.
  Result: 44 -> 37 edges over 6 bases, and every one is a confirmed member. Two rows deserve note because they correct me: `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` SURVIVE, because they are inherited from `EventTarget.prototype` three hops up the `HTMLElement` chain and a subclass method that shadows an inherited one genuinely overrides it. I had earlier recorded all six `HTMLElement.*` rows as false; two of them are not. That is why the table models CHAINS rather than flat lists — a flat list cannot express inheritance, and that is precisely what made my earlier number wrong.
  An unknown base keeps the 0.5 guess: declining to speak about a base we cannot resolve is the honest position, and the guess is declared as a guess.
**RESULT ON THE LANE.** Both corpora at 100% coverage, MISSING=0, unexplained=0 and heuristic=0, and the G20 label gate passes with exit 0. `heuristic` going to 0 is the clearest sign the work landed: those rows are no longer unexamined suspicion, they are adjudicated.

gaps.node_type: overrides — an ACCESSOR shadowing a base accessor is a real override the lane does not model
gaps.missing: `class A extends B { get x() {} }` where `B` has an accessor `x` does override it in JavaScript — accessor pairs are prototype members and a subclass accessor shadows the base one. The lane emits no `overrides` edge for it, because the analyzer classifies an accessor as `property` (a declared contract) and the override pass considers only Methods and Constructors.
gaps.evidence:
Found while building the J9 oracle, and recorded rather than absorbed: the oracle mirrors the accessor rule so that truth and analyzer agree, and that mirroring is LOCKSTEP ON A KNOWN OMISSION rather than a shared conviction. The distinction matters — lockstep on a rule believed right is exactly how X1 happened, and lockstep on a rule KNOWN to be incomplete is a different thing provided the incompleteness is written down.
MEASURED, and it is not a corner case. `svelte/packages/svelte/src/reactivity/url.js` declares `class SvelteURL extends URL` and then re-declares twelve `URL` members as accessor pairs — `get hash()` / `set hash(value)` and the same for `host`, `hostname`, `href`, `password`, `pathname`, `port`, `protocol`, `search` and others. Those are twelve genuine overrides of `URL.prototype` accessors, and the lane records none of them. This was discovered as 12 MISSING rows when the oracle was first built to model them, which is the clearest possible statement of the gap: the truth side derived the relationship and the analyzer did not have it.
**WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE.** The fix is to extend the override pass to accessors, which means changing a DECLARED contract — the symbol table says `get`/`set` yield `property`, and other lanes and fixtures read that. Whether an accessor should be `property` and still participate in `overrides`, or become a distinct kind, is a design question with a blast radius across the family. It is recorded so the gap is visible rather than absorbed into a lockstep.
gaps.status: CLOSED — accessors participate in `overrides`; the 12 url.js overrides are recorded and the pair collapses to one edge

decisions.node_type: accessor-slot semantics (method_definition get/set pairs)
decisions.question: M49 #758 B5: get/set pairs collapsed to ONE symbol via the owner:name J3 dedup key — the getter was deadSpanned (nested symbols pruned, body calls skipped) and the setter's body walked under the getter's slot. Also: what happens when a DATA member shares the name (get x + x())?
decisions.decision: RULED - FIXED: accessor pairs are DISTINCT descriptor slots (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor returns {get, set}) — both Property symbols survive with metadata.accessorKind, and BOTH bodies walk (calls/uses/symbols). Runtime slot semantics kept honest: a DATA member REPLACES the whole descriptor slot (get x then x() kills the accessor entirely — both halves removed, bodies deadSpanned); an accessor takes over a data member's slot; get+set MERGE (coexist). Cross-kind kills are post-walk zombies (mid-walk splice would corrupt seenMethodIdx indices). Pinned by javascript/accessor-slot-semantics + 3 mutants (accessor-pair-collapse, data-slot-zombie, static-override-fabrication).

decisions.question: M49 W1: the javascript lane reported 100/0/0 while both sides fabricated uses for binding positions. Oracle lockstep (the C5 standing lesson) mirrored a defect instead of catching it. What stops a lane from agreeing on a wrong contract?
decisions.decision: RULED - a lane cannot independently verify a surface whose truth is mirrored from the same contract. Two guards: (1) F9-PROBE-JSD-BINDINGS runs with oracleForbid enabled, so an oracle that derives a forbidden edge fails the battery as `oracle colludes` (new probeLang capability, reusable by every future probe; self-tested by re-introducing the fabrication and watching it fail); (2) every analyzer behavior change must be pinned by an F3 fixture asserting the SEMANTIC contract (forbidden edges), not only by lane counts.

decisions.node_type: member-chain assignment LHS (write) — subtree vs node suppression
decisions.question: M49 W1: `document.getElementById(id).style.display = v` lost the read of `id` and of `style`, and `store.inner.limit = v` lost `store`/`inner`. The suppression used `continue` in a stack walk that pushes children at the loop tail, so the whole STATEMENT SUBTREE was skipped. What does a write suppress?
decisions.decision: RULED - the write LHS suppresses ONLY its own target node, never the subtree. Reads nested inside the statement (call arguments, intermediate chain segments, the RHS) must survive; the write target itself (`limit`, `display`) must not emit a read. Implemented as a per-node guard (`if (!isWrite)`) so the tail child-push still runs. Pinned by fixture javascript/write-lhs-nested-reads with two mutants (write-lhs-subtree-skip, write-target-read-leak). Found only because the #760 cold-pool rotation sampled never-sampled files (grails-core MISSING=7, lodash MISSING=26) - no fixture had ever covered the shape, and the code comment asserted the opposite of what it did.

decisions.node_type: member-chain head in call-rooted chains
decisions.question: M49 W1: for a call-rooted chain the head was emitted as raw node TEXT, so `document.getElementById(id).style = v` produced `uses -> document.getElementById(id)` — a target that is not a symbol. Emit or not?
decisions.decision: RULED - the chain head is a read only when it IS an identifier (the chain-root contract). A call/literal head carries no symbol; the call already has its `calls` edge. Analyzer + oracle gated identically; pinned by javascript/write-lhs-nested-reads (`targetEndsWith` forbid) and mutant javascript/chain-head-expression-fabrication.

decisions.node_type: member identity inside object literals (dedup scope)
decisions.question: M49 W2 (#769): the method dedup key was `${owner ?? "module"}:${name}` and scopeOwnerName only reports CLASS scopes, so every object-literal member of a module shared ONE slot. Two init()s in sibling objects, or two Vue prop-default() factories, collapsed: the later replaced the earlier, dead-spanning its body and dropping its calls. Is a member's identity its bare name in the module?
decisions.decision: RULED - NO. Identity is CONTAINER-SCOPED: class body -> class name (unchanged), object literal -> the literal's span (obj@<startIndex>). Sibling containers never collide; duplicates INSIDE one container still collapse last-wins (J3 + the dup-key Option A ruling) because they share the key. Also fixed the B5 sibling-accessor kill, which matched owner+name TEXT and so also killed same-named accessors of OTHER object literals - it now resolves the exact sibling slot key. Analyzer-only (the JS lane truth oracle derives both calls site-agnostically, so lockstep was already correct here); pinned by javascript/sibling-object-member-identity (init count=2 + calls init->one) and mutants javascript/sibling-object-collapse, vue/prop-default-multi-collapse.

decisions.node_type: fixture authoring from a corpus file (process, not a grammar shape)
decisions.question: M49 W2: #762 closed as `verified ALREADY-FIXED` on vue/prop-default-factory-calls - a fixture with ONE factory, whose assertions pass with or without the sibling-object collision - while the corpus file (MarkdownEditor) kept MISSING={toFixed,random}. What must a corpus-derived fixture reproduce?

A one-factory reconstruction of a two-factory file tested an adjacent shape and produced false confidence for two waves. Re-authored vue/prop-default-factory-calls to the real shape (two sibling factories + interleaved plain `default:` members) and verified it FAILS against the pre-fix code (mutant vue/prop-default-multi-collapse) before accepting the green.

decisions.node_type: template_substitution (read positions)
decisions.question: M49 W4 rotated-sample finding (ledger J6): the template-substitution walk emitted Uses for EVERY identifier in the substitution subtree, so ${fn(x)} fabricated `uses fn` and ${obj.m(x)} fabricated `uses obj` - 5 corpus edges (benchmarking/utils.js, transform-template/template.js) that the F5 truth rightly refused; the walk's own sibling rule nine lines up excludes callees (!isCallee).
decisions.decision: RULED - a substituted identifier is a read only when it is not part of a call's callee expression and not an assignment target; the walk gates on ancestor containment (call `function` span / assignment `left` span) and, per the TS TSD28 family contract, owns the substitution read alone (the general bare-read rule's duplicate is suppressed: one interpolated read = ONE Uses edge at 0.85 isTemplateInterpolation). Analyzer-only fix; the oracle already excluded callees, so parity was restored, not negotiated.
decisions.evidence: fixture javascript/template-substitution-reads (forbid uses fn/obj + count==1); mutants javascript/template-callee-uses + javascript/template-read-duplicate CAUGHT; F3 javascript 55/55; F4 full battery 449/449 (0 survivors); corpus re-probe at the fixed tree: svelte-repo javascript lane 0 unexplained (was 5)

decisions.node_type: class (class EXPRESSION) member identity
decisions.question: M49 W13 (deep-measurement finding; W12 residual): only class_declaration pushed a Class scope, so scopeOwnerName returned undefined for every member of every ANONYMOUS class expression and they ALL shared the dedup key `module:<name>` - the second class expression's `constructor` (and any same-named method) replaced the first, dead-spanning its body and dropping every edge it owned. Measured on the svelte corpus: custom-element.js defines TWO class expressions (the SvelteElement custom-element base, and the per-component Class inside create_custom_element), each with a constructor, so this.attachShadow(shadow_root_init) in the FIRST vanished - the second javascript-lane MISSING edge W12's 400-file measurement registered. The 60-file rotation never sampled a file with two anonymous class expressions, which is why the deep run found it and no fixture did.
decisions.decision: RULED - a member's identity is container-scoped (W2 #769 for object literals, now class bodies too): when no declared class name exists, the containing class_body's span is the container key. Duplicates INSIDE one class still collapse last-wins (J3 / dup-key Option A). Pinned by fixture javascript/class-expression-member-identity (constructor count=2, run count=2, calls constructor->attachShadow and calls run->alpha - both LOST pre-fix) with mutant javascript/class-expression-container-collapse.

decisions.node_type: member_expression with private_property_identifier (read positions)
decisions.question: M49 W13 (deep-measurement finding; W12 residual): the member-segment dedup key was `${source}.${seg}`, and a private segment's text is literally `#x` - so the key became `${source}.#` + `x`, BYTE-IDENTICAL to the bare-read/chain-root key of the plain identifier `x` (`${source}.#` + `x`). Whichever node was walked first claimed it. Measured on the svelte corpus: packages/svelte/src/reactivity/set.js - the field initializer `#update_version = update_version || -1` (line 52) reads the IMPORTED binding update_version first, claiming key SvelteSet.#update_version, so the genuine read this.#update_version (line 88) was dropped as a duplicate - the FIRST javascript-lane MISSING edge W12's 400-file measurement registered. #version/#size survived only because no plain binding of those names is read in the same container.
decisions.decision: RULED - a private segment's key uses a `#`-marked namespace (`${source}.$private${seg}`); `#` cannot appear inside an identifier, so no bare/root/segment key can collide with it and the private read and the same-named bare read are distinct edges that never suppress each other. The emitted target keeps the `#` spelling. Pinned by fixture javascript/private-member-read-identity (uses Store->#update_version LOST pre-fix) with mutant javascript/private-read-key-collision.

decisions.node_type: ERROR, MISSING
decisions.question: F8 re-audit: the census injects ERROR and MISSING into every language's node-type set (completeness-inventory.ts:609 — they are not in the wasm symbol table, so the gate adds them by hand), yet no javascript spec row claimed them, so section-a failed for javascript and for 10+ other lanes on the same pair. Gap, silent omission, or handled?
decisions.decision: RULED - HANDLED, and this is the javascript analog of bash BD5 (which the gate's own comment at completeness-inventory.ts:601-608 cites as the precedent: 'a spec that classifies ERROR - correctly, since the analyzer consults it - was being told its own row was grammar drift ... the fix is never to delete the correct row'). javascript holds an EXPLICIT guard, real-javascript-analyzer.ts:302: `if (n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing)`, which records a warning on result.errors and skips the damaged subtree. ERROR is therefore handled_verified: the analyzer consults it on purpose, exactly as bash does at real-bash-analyzer.ts:663/703/715. The guard is SCOPED to the damaged region, never a blanket file refusal - the property BD5 insists on, because a blanket refusal swallows valid declarations in a partially broken file. Measured at f10ea18f: `function good(){} function bad( { } const x = ;` -> good:function SURVIVES; the same file with the damage first -> BOTH x:constant and good:function survive; `function good(){} const arr = [1, 2` (unterminated) -> good:function survives, the array yielding only uses:T->arr. A clean control emits the same good:function with no errors, and a wholly-damaged file yields symbols:[] with one warning per ERROR. MISSING is filed internal_silent: the same guard reports it, but it contributes no symbol of its own. No fabrication is possible here - an unresolved name stays unresolved.

decisions.node_type: implements (relationship type — the lane's only UNEMITTED ontology member)
decisions.question: docs/analyzers/ONTOLOGY-WORKSTREAM.md Part 2: every one of the ten relationship types needs a measured verdict. `implements` is the one this analyzer does not emit. Is it a GAP (the language has the construct) or RULED (it does not)? Prose is not sufficient — `overrides` was missing from Bash for a whole wave behind a prose justification and it was wrong — so this records the four INSTRUMENTS and their numbers.
decisions.resolution: RULED — THE LANGUAGE HAS NO `implements` CLAUSE (2026-10-03), and the ruling is falsifiable by a probe finding a non-zero count. Four independent instruments, all measured on the production parse of every admitted js-family file: (A) GRAMMAR INVENTORY — the pinned tree-sitter-javascript 0.23.1 wasm produced 187 distinct node types over svelte's 3,447 real JavaScript files and 140 over lodash's 51, and NONE of them is an implements/supertype clause node (`implements_clause`, `superclass`, `interface_declaration`, `extends_clause` are all absent from the observed vocabulary; 220 distinct types over the 13,202-file typescript corpus, same result). (B) PARSE-TREE COUNT — every `class_heritage` clause read: svelte has 18, ALL of shape `identifier`, the only anonymous token under `class_heritage` anywhere is `extends` (18 occurrences, 1:1 with the clauses), and the `implements` token occurs 0 times; lodash has 0 heritage clauses; the 13,202-file corpus has 4,428 clauses with the same 1:1 `extends` ratio and 0 `implements` tokens. (C) The 97 `class_heritage` clauses in that corpus with more than one named child are ALL inside an ERROR node (`ERROR+identifier` 86, `ERROR+binary_expression` 11) in files that do not parse — `extends A, B` and `extends Control implements SelectableControl` are TypeScript EMIT baselines written to a `.js` path, i.e. syntax the JavaScript grammar rejects. A multi-supertype clause is what `implements` looks like where a language has one, and this grammar cannot represent one at all. (D) The one place the JS ECOSYSTEM spells the word is a COMMENT: 45 `@implements` JSDoc tags in 9 files on the typescript corpus, every one of the nine a `tsc/testdata/baselines/` file, and 1 tag on svelte. A comment is not the language; this lane's standing contract (see D1) keeps type information ABSENT rather than synthetic, and an `implements` edge read out of a doc comment would name an interface no program declares. So: RULED, with the falsifier stated — a probe that finds an `implements` token under `class_heritage`, or a supertype-shaped node type in the grammar inventory, overturns it. THE ARBITER'S OWN FRESH VERDICT (2026-10-12, `ontology-coverage-gate.ts javascript --fresh`, 12,805/12,805 files NEWLY WALKED, 0 resumed - the gate refuses by design to adjudicate a checkpoint it did not parse, and its `--coverage` mode is a preamble that exits before any table): `implements` reads `RULED-SOUND - NOT EMITTED; the grammar produced 215 distinct node types across the corpus and NONE expresses it`, the other nine read `EMITTED` with live edge counts (`calls` 643,407 / `uses` 511,573 / `contains` 31,832 / `exports` 28,366 / `imports` 18,813 / `instantiates` 9,275 / `extends` 2,443 / `overrides` 1,475 / `references` 1,397), and the verdict line is `emitted 9/10 ruled-sound 1 FALSIFIED 0 ruled-without-justification 0` - so nothing is claimed inapplicable that is derivable and nothing is silent without a ruling.
decisions.decision:
RULED — see `resolution` for the four instruments and their counts. Cross-check: `script/m60/rel-type-coverage-gate.ts` reads javascript's emitted set as the 9 types it constructs and its audited set as all 10, so `implements` is compared and absent rather than uncompared and absent — the shape a wrong ruling usually hides behind. That gate needs a `JAVASCRIPT_RULED` table entry for `implements` (instrument A) to print RULED-SOUND instead of RULED-UNJUSTIFIED; the table is `script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts`, which is shared and therefore reported rather than edited.

[UNION: the version from the other side read — RULED — see `resolution` for the four instruments and their counts. Cross-check: `script/m60/rel-type-coverage-gate.ts` reads javascript's emitted set as the 9 types it constructs and its audited set as all 10, so `implements` is compared and absent rather than uncompared and absent — the shape a wrong ruling usually hides behind. That table entry now EXISTS (2026-10-08): `script/m14/javascript-ruled.ts`, exported as `JAVASCRIPT_RULED` and registered as `RULED_BY_LANG.javascript` in `script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts`, so the gate adjudicates `implements` on instrument A over the four node types rather than on spec prose; `script/m14/verify-ruling-tables-registered.ts` fails loudly if the file and the registry ever disagree.]

decisions.node_type: class (class expression) → class_heritage → extends
decisions.question: The differential's truth derives `extends` from EVERY `class_heritage` clause, while the analyzer's `class` case needs a name to attach the edge to and stays silent without one. Two binding shapes reach that silence: a MEMBER-EXPRESSION binding (`globalThis.MutationObserver = class extends MutationObserver {…}`, where the class IS bound but not to a bare identifier) and NO binding at all. Measured: is the first a gap?
decisions.resolution: RULED — BOTH SHAPES STAY SILENT (2026-10-03), and the member-binding shape is 1 of 18 heritage clauses on svelte and 3 of 3,977 on the 13,202-file typescript corpus (0.075%). Every heritage clause in each corpus was classified by the binding shape above it (`script/m14/tmp/js-class-heritage-coverage.ts`): svelte 12 named declarations, 1 class expression with its own name, 2 identifier-bound expressions, 1 member-bound expression, 2 unbound; typescript 3,170 / 663 / 45 / 3 / 96. Two reasons the member-bound form is not implemented rather than merely small. (1) `a.b = class extends X` is an ASSIGNMENT, not a declaration: this lane's symbol contract publishes symbols for declarations, so the class has no symbol, and an `extends` edge whose source is the written path `globalThis.MutationObserver` resolves to nothing — the R10 spelling rule (`validation/m60/target-spelling-register.json`) requires an endpoint to be spelled the way the lane would publish that name as a symbol, and `globalThis.MutationObserver` is not. Publishing `extends MutationObserver -> MutationObserver` instead would be a self-loop on a monkey-patch, which says less than silence. (2) The unbound form is already the lane's DECLARED behaviour: `javascript/class-expression-heritage` pins `runIt(class extends Base {})` as producing no edge, because nothing in the language names it. The known consequence is stated rather than hidden: the truth side derives those rows, so they surface as MISSING in the differential — measured at 1 row on a 120-file svelte draw (`extends -> Svelte4Component` from `legacy-client.js:52`) and 6 MISSING rows over a 600-file draw, against a recorded baseline of 0.
decisions.decision: RULED — silent for the member-bound and unbound shapes; the cost is a measured MISSING count, quoted above. The rule that would have to change is `bindingNameAbove` (real-javascript-analyzer.ts), which accepts only a bare `identifier` on the left of an assignment.

decisions.node_type: R7 runtime half — relationship endpoints and symbol names
decisions.question: Standing rule R7 has a STATIC census (a placeholder literal at a source site) and an unfinished RUNTIME half (no emitted row may carry a placeholder or an empty string as a name). This lane has ZERO registered R7 sites statically, and the census that found the class was written by a previous round. Did the runtime half hold?
decisions.resolution: RULED — NO, AND IT DID NOT. Three defects, all measured on the production entry (`pool-worker.parseFile`), all now FIXED in this lane's analyzer (2026-10-03). (1) 2,037 of 356,490 edges on the 13,202-file corpus carried an EMPTY source or target, every one produced by tree-sitter's error recovery writing a zero-length node: 1,934 `uses` rows reading a zero-length `identifier`, 87 `uses` rows whose member-chain segment was empty, 5 template substitutions written `${ }`, 7 `uses` rows with an empty SOURCE (the source expression read `method ?? owner ?? moduleName`, and `??` does not fall through an empty string), 3 `calls` rows on an empty callee, 1 `exports` row whose CJS surface segment was empty. FIXED by a terminal guard that drops any row with an empty endpoint, mirroring the guard `script/m14/differential.ts` already applies to its TRUTH side (M60/SDJ-17) — which is why the comparison was asymmetric: the truth could not assert an unnameable edge and the analyzer could publish one. (2) `extractInstanceofRefs.resolveSource` returned the literal `global`, publishing a `references` row from a symbol name no file contains: 14 rows on lodash's 51 ES5 files and 1 on svelte — REAL JavaScript, not recovery residue, which is why no clean-corpus gate saw it. FIXED by sourcing to the module, the convention `extractExportRelationships` and the `uses` walk already apply. (3) `collectPatternPairs` pushed a module-scope destructuring binding with no length check, so a zero-length `identifier` became a symbol named the empty string: 32 symbols over 115,356, every one a reserved word used as a binding; FIXED by requiring a writable name. After the fixes the same measurements read 0, 0 and 0 (115,356 → 115,324 symbols). decisions.node_type: import_statement → import_clause → identifier (a binding that is not a symbol)
decisions.question: An ESM import binds a NAME in the file (`import text from './text.js'`), but this lane's family contract publishes no symbol for an import binding, so nothing in the symbol table is named `text`. Two systems then disagree about whether that name exists. Measured on the lane's own corpora, this is not hypothetical: how many edges does the disagreement cost, and where does it happen?
decisions.resolution: RULED — IT IS NOT THE LANE'S NOISE, IT IS A SHARED FILTER (2026-10-03), and the lane's own output is correct at every step. `RealJavaScriptAnalyzer.analyze` on `import text from './text.js'` publishes `imports <module> -> ./text.js:text` and `uses f -> text` (probed through the class directly), and so does `ASTEngine.parseFile`. The production indexer, `src/ast/pool-worker.ts` `parseFile`, then runs `filterNoiseRelationships`, whose `NOISE_TARGETS` set contains `text` because `text` is a web-tree-sitter Node accessor. The set's escape hatch — a name the FILE DECLARES survives — cannot fire for an import binding, because a binding is not a declaration this lane publishes. Measured cost of that one word in the set: on svelte 600 files the production entry delivers 36,261 of the engine's 36,731 relationships, deleting **470 (1.28%)**: 466 `uses`, 2 `calls`, 1 `imports`, 1 `exports`, with deleted targets `type` 343, `parent` 97, `text` 15, `lastChild` 6, `firstChild` 4, `nextSibling` 2. On lodash's 51 files it deletes **31 of 21,063 (0.15%)**: `type` 12, `text` 9, `parent` 4, `lastChild` 3, `firstChild` 2, `startIndex` 1. Those are real reads and real calls of ordinary JavaScript property names — `lib/main/build-site.js` really calls a function named `text`, and minified lodash really reads `.type`. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, and this is the part that generalises: `script/m14/differential.ts` measures the javascript lane through `ASTEngine.parseFile` (differential.ts:22090), so every differential figure describes the UNFILTERED path, while the product indexes through the pool worker. A lane can therefore report 0 unexplained, 100% covered and 0 MISSING while the graph a user queries is missing rows. The per-label instrument in `script/m14/javascript-label-oracle-agreement.ts` sees it from the other side: on lodash it reports 21 MISSING rows against 0 on the harness, and every one of the 21 is a row the filter deleted (2 `calls` to `text`/`parent`, 19 `uses` to `type`/`text`/`parent`).
decisions.decision: RULED — the lane's analyzer is correct and the loss is in shared code this lane does not own; the fix and the two-line oracle-side note are REPORTED, not made. What this lane can and does own is the consequence for its own verdict table: `imports` and `uses` rows naming `text`/`type`/`parent`/`firstChild`/`lastChild`/`nextSibling`/`startIndex` are CORRECT emissions, so they must not be read as fabrications in a resolution census — a resolution instrument that lists those tokens as placeholders convicts the lane for being right, which is the same over-counting error this decision exists to stop. AMENDED (2026-10-10) — THE FIX IS NOW MADE, in `src/ast/pool-worker.ts`, and the analysis above is kept as the reasoning that forced it rather than as the current state. Two parts. (1) THE BINDING HATCH: `importBindingNames()` builds the set of names the file BINDS, and `filterNoiseRelationships` takes it as a fourth argument, so a binding reaches the escape hatch that only a declaration could reach before; the hatch is also tested on the LEAF, because an `imports` row's target is path-spelled (`./text.js:text`) and a set of symbol names can never equal that string — two independent reasons the documented case could not be admitted. (2) THE COLLISION RULE: what remained was 354 lost rows on the svelte 600-file sample and 21 on lodash, and the discriminator is recorded by the ANALYZER, not guessed from the name — a noise-named target the analyzer recorded as a read it derived from source structure (`metadata.isFieldAccess`, a dotted `metadata.calleeExpression`, or `metadata.isTemplateInterpolation`) is a real read, while a leak (an analyzer passing `node.type` where a symbol name belongs) carries no marker at all and is still refused. The rule is scoped to the JS family through `NOISE_TARGET_FAMILIES` and does not touch the universal test-lifecycle group. CURRENT NUMBERS, all through the production entry (`pool-worker.parseFile`), all re-measured after the change: two-path loss svelte 600 files 354 of 36,881 -> 0, lodash 51 files 21 of 20,898 -> 0, ts corpus 1,500 files 4 lost (three index-signature `contains` targets and one multiline `instanceof` recovery target — deleted by the universal IDENTIFIER sanitizer, not by NOISE_TARGETS, so a different defect class, named and not folded in), gained 0 at every step on every corpus. The per-label instrument reads `uses` truth 10,602 / analyzer 10,602 / covered 10,602 / MISSING 0 and `imports` MISSING 0 on svelte-600 (was 214 and 19, all filter deletions), and lodash-51 MISSING 0 on every label with fabrication 0. PINNED BY `script/m14/js-ontology/js-filter-hatch-probe.ts` (15 cases, exit 0; falsified 3-fail with the collision rule disabled and 4-fail with the bound-names hatch disabled, file restored byte-identically by sha256 after each). CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN INSTRUMENT: the ladder was first recorded as 378/16/0 and 4/0, measured while the two-path instrument asked the filter with only the LANGUAGE argument while production passes the per-file declared and bound names too; that configuration counted rows production keeps as lost, which the svelte artifact showed directly (`imports 2 lost` on a sample where production had lost none). Every figure above is from the corrected instrument.

decisions.node_type: class_heritage / implements_clause / interface_declaration (the grammar's DECLARED vocabulary, not a corpus sample)

A corpus is a sample of the world's files, so a ruling resting only on a sample is a ruling about the sample. What does the pinned GRAMMAR PACKAGE itself declare, and can the instrument be shown to fire on a grammar that does have the construct?

No `implements_clause`, no `interface_declaration`, and `grep -c implements grammar.js` is 0. That is a fact about the PARSER, not about which files happen to be checked out. (A2) THE PROBE IS SHOWN TO FIRE: the identical scan over `node_modules/tree-sitter-typescript/typescript/src/node-types.json` returns 183 named types including `implements_clause`, `interface_declaration`, `interface_body`, `abstract_class_declaration` and `abstract_method_signature`. So the falsifier is a single structural predicate: a real multi-supertype clause is a `class_heritage` with more than one named child and NO ERROR anywhere in it. Measured: 0 on svelte (18 clauses, 0 multi), 0 on lodash (0 clauses), 97 on the ts corpus and ALL 97 are inside an ERROR node, produced by `extends (0, __extends)(A, B)` helper output and `extends A, B`, neither of which is JavaScript. CORRECTION carried from this round: the census instrument reported "multi-supertype clauses 8" on the ts corpus because `heritageMulti` was capped at 8 and its LENGTH was printed as the count. The census now keeps a separate counter carrying the ERROR flag, so a cap can never again be read as a measurement. This round's own ruling instrument repeated the same cap in its first version (it printed 40) and is fixed the same way; recorded rather than quietly corrected because an instrument that caps and prints the cap as a count is the exact failure this workstream exists to catch.

decisions.node_type: comment -> `@implements {Type}` (JSDoc; not a node the grammar has)
decisions.question: JSD33 counted JSDoc `@implements` tags and called them comments. "It is a comment" is half an argument, because a comment CAN still carry a real edge. The decisive question is whether such an edge could ever RESOLVE: JavaScript declares no interfaces and no abstract classes as a separate kind, so `@implements {IFoo}` names a type with no declaration site in the language. If no corpus tag names a declared symbol, implementing the tag would produce a graph of unbindable targets — a decoration, not a relationship. Measured?
decisions.resolution: RULED — MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, and the measurement decides the ruling rather than decorating it. Instrument F counts `@implements` tags and asks, for every type a tag names, whether ANY JavaScript file in the corpus declares a symbol of that name. svelte: 1 tag, 0 types named, 0 declared. The single tag is `packages/svelte/src/compiler/utils/compile_diagnostic.js:50` `@implements {ICompileDiagnostic}`, and `ICompileDiagnostic` is declared in `packages/svelte/src/compiler/types/index.d.ts` — a TYPESCRIPT declaration file, whose only mention in any `.js` in that repository is the JSDoc tag itself. ts corpus: 45 tags (31 in comments attached to no symbol, the rest inside compiler-emit baselines), 0 declared. lodash: 0 tags. So across 16,699 admitted JavaScript files there is not one `@implements` tag whose target a JavaScript file declares. Three further reasons, each measured rather than rhetorical: (1) the construct is not in the tree — it is comment text, so deriving it means writing a JSDoc parser this lane has deliberately declined for `@param`, `@returns` and `@type` alike, on the stated ground that JavaScript has no runtime types; (2) the language has nowhere to put the edge, per JSD38's counterfactual; (3) the emitted edge would be unresolvable at both ends by construction, per this instrument. Instrument: `script/m14/javascript-implements-ruling.ts`, instruments D and F.

decisions.node_type: import_statement -> the import RECORD's local binding and type (brain_import.imported_as / import_type)
decisions.question: The lane's `implements`-style gap rows are closed, but the STORE's view of a javascript import was never checked the way the edges were. `brain_import` has an `imported_as` column and a `patterns.ts` consumer that computes unused imports as `usedName = imported_as || imported_name`; the lane emits the local binding on every form. What does the store actually receive, and what does a consumer see?
decisions.resolution: RULED — IT RECEIVED THE MODULE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE, and this one is the lane's own seam. Read back out of a real index (`packages/svelte/src`, 368 files, through `indexProjectParallel`): every javascript import row was `imported_name = './wrapper/wrapper_bench.js'` (the MODULE), `imported_as = NULL` (the local binding, dropped), `import_type = 'named'` — including `import x from './m'` and `import * as ns from './m'`. Two independent causes, both measured rather than inferred. (1) The worker's BasicImport mapping emitted neither `localName` nor the key the store reads for the type, while `parallel-indexer`'s insert reads `imp.alias ?? imp.localName` for `imported_as` and `imp.importType ?? (isDefault ? "default" : isNamespace ? "namespace" : "named")` for `import_type` — and this lane spells the type in `type`, not `importType`. (2) `import * as w from './warnings.js'` published NO binding anywhere: the analyzer's import record carried `items: ["*"]` and the alias `w` was in the tree but in no field. CONSUMER CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is not cosmetic: `src/ast/patterns.ts` looks `usedName` up IN THE FILE, so for this lane it searched for a module specifier the source never writes — every javascript import was reportable as unused. EVIDENCE PATH: all four forms parsed through the production entry and printed, and the same four forms indexed through `indexProjectParallel` on a two-file project and read back from `brain_import`.
decisions.decision: RULED AND FIXED in this lane's own files (2026-10-10), no shared column semantics changed. `src/ast/real-javascript-analyzer.ts` publishes three parallel arrays per import statement — `bindings` (the LOCAL name for every form, including the namespace alias), `declaredNames` and `kinds` — plus `namespaceName`, so the filter's escape hatch also counts a namespace binding as a name the file BINDS. `src/ast/pool-worker.ts` emits `localName` and `importType` per ITEM, which is what the store already reads; per-item rather than per-statement, so `import a, { b } from './m'` no longer labels both items with the statement's single `isDefault` flag. After the fix, on the same two-file index: `thing`/default, `alpha`/named, `bee`/named (`beta as bee`), `ns`/namespace, and the side-effect import still binds nothing. PINNED BY `script/m14/verify-js-import-seam.ts` — 8 checks, exit 0, run through the real indexer rather than the mapping — and FALSIFIED: with both halves of the fix removed it reads 5 of 8 failing (the four binding/type checks and the knock-on), with the files restored byte-identically by sha256. NOT CHANGED, and pinned as such by the same gate: `imported_name` still carries the MODULE SPECIFIER for this record shape. The column's meaning differs per lane (module-shaped records put the module there), so changing it is a fleet-wide call and not this lane's; the gate pins the current value so a future change is visible. STILL OPEN, measured and named: the binding-level RESOLUTION route this fix unblocks — 2,581 rows on the closed 368-file population name a symbol the row's own file imports, which the store's name-uniqueness strategies cannot see (`script/m14/javascript-import-decidability.ts`).

decisions.node_type: import_statement -> brain_import ROW IDENTITY (one row per imported name, not per statement)
decisions.question: A clause that imports several names is one statement and several bindings. What does the store keep?
decisions.resolution: RULED — IT KEPT THE LAST ONE AND DROPPED THE REST, fleet-wide, and this is the shared-insert seam of the resolution work rather than a lane-local one. `parallel-indexer` keyed the row `${fileId}:import:${module}:${line}` and wrote it with `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so every member of one clause collided on that key and only the final member survived. MEASURED on the closed `packages/svelte/src` population (368 files, read back from `brain_import`): `internal/client/reactivity/create-subscriber.js` writes `{ get, tick, untrack }`, `{ effect_tracking, render_effect }` and `{ source, increment }` and the store held exactly `untrack`, `render_effect`, `increment`. The cost is not cosmetic: a binding the store never recorded is a binding NO RESOLVER CAN READ, so the rows naming `get`, `source` and `tick` kept the name pass's answer (`source` on `compiler/preprocess/index.js`, `get` on `compiler/phases/scope.js`) with no evidence left to correct them against. The identifier is not a contract — nothing in `src/` parses it and `deleteFileImports` clears a file's rows before a reindex, so only intra-file uniqueness is required — and the imported name is the right discriminator. A lane publishing neither `alias`, `localName` nor `name` keeps its historical id exactly.
decisions.decision: FIXED 2026-10-10 in `src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts` (the row id now carries the imported name). Gate: `script/m14/verify-js-binding-resolution.ts` B7 asserts that EVERY binding of every clause of a five-binding, multi-clause file is stored (`['aliased:named','helper:named','ns:namespace','p2:named','parse:named']`) and B8 that a call through the SECOND member of a clause lands on the right symbol; both ran through `indexProjectParallel`. FALSIFIED: with the row id restored to the module+line form the same gate reads that set as `['ns','p2']`. FLEET BENEFIT, measured rather than asserted: the fixture suite's groovy lane goes 20 failures to 2 on this change alone (every other lane's counts identical, javascript 76/0), which is what a shared-insert fix looks like when it is the actual cause.

decisions.node_type: bare-name edge target whose name is a PARAMETER of the row's own source symbol (shadowed local binding)
decisions.question: The name passes always produce an answer for a bare name. What is the right state for a row whose name is a local parameter — `import { get } from './m'` followed by `export function toStore(get, set)`?
decisions.resolution: RULED — THE ATTACHMENT IS PROVABLY WRONG AND MUST BE CLEARED, not left and not 'corrected' onto the import. A parameter of the row's own source symbol is in scope at every statement of its body by construction, so the name cannot be the imported symbol; and it is not the import either, because the parameter shadows it. MEASURED on the closed population: `store/index-server.js` declares `export function toStore(get, set)` while importing `get`, and its two `get` call rows were attached to `compiler/phases/scope.js:get`; `batch.js` declares `capture(source, value, is_derived)` and its `source` row landed on `compiler/preprocess/index.js:source` — a file that does not own the name in scope at all. Seven rows on that population, every one a confident lie in `bb_graph`, `bb_impact` and hover. An unresolved edge is honest; the lane's posture decides this.
decisions.decision: FIXED 2026-10-10 in `src/ast/binding-resolution.ts` (the shadow gate now emits a DETACH decision — `shadowed-local-binding` — and the pass clears `target_symbol_id`, counting the row as `detached` in its outcome, which `parallel-indexer` logs). Gate: `verify-js-binding-resolution.ts` A6 pins the planner decision and B9 pins the store state for a real `export function shadowed(parse) { return parse() }` through `indexProjectParallel`. PAIRED MEASUREMENT: `script/m14/javascript-import-landing.ts` withholds a shadowed name from its denominator (recomputing expectations FROM THE SOURCE, never from the resolver's return value), so the two instruments agree on 3,093 import-decidable rows rather than one of them counting rows the import statement cannot decide.

decisions.question: `keepSymbol` was measured and corrected, and its comment records the measurement. A name the source literally writes and a consumer literally imports was still absent from the store. What drops it, and how many other names are in the same state?
decisions.resolution: RULED — THE STORE PATH REFUSED A DIFFERENT LIST THAN THE PARSE PATH, so correcting one left the refusal in force one layer down where nothing reports it. `export function self(fn)` at `packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/legacy/event-modifiers.js:27` is published by the analyzer, passes `keepSymbol`, and appeared in NO `brain_symbol` row project-wide; on a single-file index the same file reads PARSE 8 / STORE 7, and 8/8 after the fix. Only the FIRST had been measured (R 12 symbols across 9 files, graphql 1 of 8,796 — `Query.me` —, sql 3 of 18,325, lua 236 declarations leaving 677 edges naming nothing, hcl H10, solidity's store-vs-analyzer divergence), and the other three kept refusing `self`, `Self`, `me`, `My`, `root`, `program`, `source_file` anyway. decisions.node_type: a bare-name edge whose symbol a file publishes WITHOUT declaring (re-export clause: `export { a } from './m'`, `export { a as b } from './m'`)
decisions.question: `import { tick } from './index-client.js'` is a binding to a BARREL. Which module declares `tick` — and can that be answered, or is the row undecidable by construction?
decisions.resolution: RULED — ANSWERABLE, and the analyzer had already published the evidence: an `imports` edge with `metadata.isReExport: true`, the source module as the specifier, the name THAT module declares (`declaredName`) and, when the clause renames, `metadata.exportedAs`. Following the CLAUSE is what makes it exact; the `exports` edge beside it was aimed at the wrong module and would have inherited the error (measured: `internal/client/index.js` publishes `pop` from `./context.js` and its edge held `compiler/phases/1-parse/index.js:pop`, its `add_svelte_meta` edge a compiler visitor). Two actions shipped together, both through the same clause channel: an `exports` row that declares nothing locally is re-targeted at the module the clause names, and a consumer row whose target file is a barrel follows the same chain (depth-bounded at 8, cycle-guarded by (file, name)) to the declarer; a module declaring the name twice at any hop refuses, because an ambiguous answer is not one this pass stores. MEASURED on the closed 368-file `packages/svelte/src` population, both arms in one session on the same draw, the unwired arm being a one-line early return in `resolveThroughReexports` restored byte-identically (sha256 `12adfbf6dfbe447f970b0a437b130fe95dc9c531d7952855e84fa6014be01a7a`): ALL import-decidable rows 3,097 of 3,099 (99.9% — 1 wrong-file, 1 no-symbol) -> 3,099 of 3,099 (100%); the `reexport` route 4 landed + 1 wrong-file + 1 no-symbol of 6 -> 6 of 6; clause-decidable re-export EDGES 209 landed / 56 wrong-file / 5 detached of 270 -> 270 of 270 with 0 wrong and 0 detached. So the chain closes 63 stored facts: 61 edge targets (56 pointing at a wrong file, 5 detached) and 2 consumer rows, named — `reactivity/window/index.js -> get` held `compiler/phases/scope.js:get` instead of `internal/client/runtime.js:get`, and `reactivity/date.js -> derived` (alias, `user_derived as derived`) held `deriveds.js:derived` instead of `deriveds.js:user_derived`. NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THE CHAIN: the instrument's decidable total reads 3,099 here against the 3,093 recorded in the JSD43 round, and 3,099 - 6 equals 3,093 exactly, which is consistent with these six rows having been unclassified before the route existed rather than with a population move; the JSD43 round's separate 'pass unwired' arm (2,796 of 3,093) was not re-run and is not the number above.
decisions.decision: FIXED 2026-10-11 in `src/ast/binding-resolution.ts` (`resolveThroughReexports` + the `reexport-chain` / `import-reexport` routes; the clause index is built from the same `imports`-edge query as the declared-name map, because they are one channel) and pinned by `script/m14/verify-js-binding-resolution.ts` — now 33 checks, 33 pass: A14 a re-exported name resolves through its own clause, A15 a TWO-HOP chain reaches the declaring module, A16 a re-export CYCLE terminates with no answer, A17 a re-export `exports` EDGE is re-targeted at the declarer, A18 two clauses publishing one name from different modules refuse, A19 a clause into a module outside the project refuses, A20 a barrel that does not publish the name refuses, B12 an aliased and a same-name re-export row land on the declarer, B13 a call through a two-hop chain lands on the declarer. FALSIFIED: 7 of the 33 gate checks fail with the chain disabled, `26 of 33` overall, and they are exactly A14 (a clause resolves), A15 (a two-hop chain), A17 (a re-export `exports` edge re-targeted), B10/B11 (renamed and same-name consumer rows), B12 (a barrel's own re-export rows) and B13 (a two-hop consumer row), restored sha-identical. The gate's summary line read a hardcoded `32` while 33 checks executed; the count is now taken from the checks that run. STILL REFUSED by construction and pinned as such: `export * as ns` keeps `path:*` at 0.6 marked unresolved because it binds a name in THIS module and redistributes nothing (the BARE `export *` form that used to be refused here is SHIPPED as of JSD46), a member the source module does not declare, a name declared twice in the source module, a chain longer than the hop budget, and a specifier that does not resolve to exactly one project file.

decisions.node_type: the two CLAUSE-LESS re-export forms — `export * from './m'` (a redistribution) and `export * as ns from './m'` (a namespace binding)
decisions.question: A barrel that writes no member name publishes names it never mentions. Can a consumer row naming one of them be decided at all — and can the two star forms be told apart, given that only one of them redistributes?
decisions.resolution: RULED — BOTH, and the second question had to be answered before the first, because the two forms emitted BYTE-IDENTICAL records. Measured through `parseFile` on one file per form: both produced the `imports` edge `./m:*` at 0.6 with `{isReExport: true, unresolved: true}` and nothing else; read back out of a real index (two-file project through `indexProjectParallel`), both produced the SAME `brain_import` row — `imported_name` = the module path, `imported_as` = NULL, `import_type` = 'named'. Two consequences, both measured: the namespace alias `ns` existed in NO field anywhere, and a resolver reading a star edge as a redistribution would have invented, for a consumer of that file, every member of `./m` the language does not export from it. The discriminator is a TREE fact, not a text guess: the grammar marks the namespace form with a NAMED `namespace_export` child (`"* as ns"`), which is also why `hasToken(node, '*')` is false for it — the `*` is inside that named node rather than a direct token, so the two forms were already taking different `items` paths before this ruling and nothing downstream could see it. RESOLUTION: the resolver follows a bare star as a STATEMENT (there is no name to file it by), carrying the SAME name to the next hop, and refuses exactly what the language refuses — `default` is never redistributed, two sources that both declare the name are ambiguous (the union is keyed by symbol, so two sources naming the same declaration still agree), a NAMED clause shadows a star for the same name, a name declared twice in a source module, a star source outside the project, and any hop that does not resolve to exactly one project file. The barrel's recorded EXPORT SURFACE deliberately does NOT gate this route: the analyzer cannot enumerate the members of a module it has not resolved, so a surface lacking the name is not evidence that the name is unpublished — the `export *` statement is. MEASURED on the closed 368-file `packages/svelte/src` population with the instrument taught the route (both arms on the same deterministic draw; the unwired arm is a one-line early return in `resolveThroughStarSources`, restored byte-identically by sha256): ALL import-decidable rows 3,099 -> **3,113 (+14)**, `not decidable by the import statement` 18,957 -> 18,943 (exactly -14), and the new `star` row reads **14 decidable / 14 landed / 0 wrong-file / 0 detached**. THE HONEST LIMIT, stated because it is the opposite of a triumph: on THIS draw the route's marginal landing count is ZERO — all 14 were already landed by the name-across-the-project strategy, because those names are unique. That is not a reason to skip the route but it is the reason the route is not sold on the draw: 263 of the draw's 2,189 distinct names ARE declared in more than one file, so the name pass has a real competitor for 12% of names and the star rows happen not to be in that set. The collision case is where the route is load-bearing, and it is pinned somewhere a draw cannot: the gate's decoy project. Also measured, and NOT built, on the census rather than on a rule of thumb: the namespace form's own member route (a consumer's `import { ns } from barrel` followed by `ns.member`, where the barrel publishes the namespace) would need the consumer's alias and would have to refuse whenever the barrel publishes more than one namespace — and the FORM ITSELF exists in exactly one corpus: typescript, 24 statements across 9 files, ALL NINE inside `tsc/testdata/baselines` (concatenated baseline dumps this lane already records as unparseable by design), against 0 in svelte, rxjs, element-plus, vuejs, shadcn-svelte, vue-element-admin and lodash. Its consumer population is 0 as well: no file in those corpora imports a name those barrels publish, so the route would ship with nothing that can exercise it. Census of the `fixtures` trees, stated as a census so it can be re-taken rather than re-argued.
decisions.decision: FIXED 2026-10-11 in `src/ast/real-javascript-analyzer.ts` (the `namespace_export` child is read, `metadata.starForm` = `all` | `namespace` is published with `namespaceName` for the namespace form, and the namespace form now publishes the per-item binding arrays a namespace IMPORT publishes — measured read back from the store: `imported_as` = 'ns', `import_type` = 'namespace', where before it was NULL and 'named') and in `src/ast/binding-resolution.ts` (`starsByFile` filed by statement, `resolveThroughStarSources` with the mechanism-tagged cycle key, `via: "import-star"`, and the namespace form excluded by `starForm`, which is REQUIRED rather than defaulted: an `imports` edge is filed as a redistribution only when it says `starForm: "all"`, because a record that does not state the form is exactly the record a guess would be wrong about — and that default is also what keeps the branch unreachable for every other lane, since no other analyzer publishes `isReExport` on an `imports` edge at all (haskell's rides an `exports` edge, nim's key is `nimReExport`, the ts lane spells it `reExport`), verified by reading those three lanes rather than by assuming it). PINNED BY: the fixture `javascript/star-reexport` (both forms, their unchanged edge spelling at `./m:*` 0.6, the new `meta.starForm`, and a `forbidRelationships` row for the pre-fix reading `./m:ns`), and `script/m14/verify-js-binding-resolution.ts` — now **46 checks, 46 pass**: A21 a redistributed name resolves, A22 a namespace member of a star barrel resolves, A23 ambiguity refused, A24 same declaration through two sources answers, A25 `default` refused, A25b the control that the same name DOES resolve through a named clause (so A25 is the star rule), A26 a named clause shadows a star, A27 a star source outside the project refused, A28 a two-hop star chain, B14 a call through a starring barrel lands on the declarer, B15 a two-hop star chain lands end to end, B16 the namespace form's binding IS stored, B17 the namespace form is NOT a redistribution (no invented edge). FALSIFIED IN TWO ARMS, each restored byte-identically by sha256: with the discriminator removed from the analyzer the gate reads **45 of 46 (B17 — the invented edge appears)** and the fixture suite reads **76 pass / 1 fail, the failure being the new fixture**; with the star route disabled the gate reads **40 of 46**, failing exactly A21, A22, A24, A28 (the positive cases; the refusals A23/A25/A26/A27 correctly still pass) and B14/B15, with the fixture suite UNAFFECTED (77/0) because the fixtures pin the analyzer and the gate pins the resolver. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THE NEW CHECKS THEMSELVES, recorded because they are the reason the checks exist: the first end-to-end run of the star cases read `attached 0` and left both rows detached, because the clause index loop skipped every `*` target BEFORE the star branch that files them (ordering, not logic); and A28 failed because the clause walk and the star walk shared one `(file, name)` cycle key, so the clause hop blocked the star hop that follows it for the same pair — the keys are now mechanism-tagged and `depth` still bounds every ping-pong.

decisions.node_type: the RESIDUE of the store graph — every detached edge row, and the definition of when one counts as resolved
decisions.question: The lane can land 100% of the rows whose target its own file declares and still leave thousands detached. Is DETACHED a defect, a boundary, or a correct refusal — and which of those is the lane still owing work on?
decisions.resolution: RULED — the state is not decidable from the count, only from a REASON, so every detached row now carries exactly one class computed from this draw alone (the row's own file, the bindings `brain_import` records for it, the engine-enumerated standard-library set, and the spelling). The classes are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by construction and their sum is printed against the total, so a class that stops matching shows up as a non-zero `unclassified` remainder rather than as a quieter total. MEASURED on the closed 250-file draw, one run of `script/m14/javascript-store-resolution.mts --files=250`: 14,336 detached rows = **1,557** source-unattributed (the OUTGOING table's population, deferred there rather than judged) + **0** label-outside-scope + **1,527** target-is-a-parameter-of-the-row's-own-source (a binding, contract-closed) + **10,464** no-binding-for-the-leaf + **255** module-is-external + **530** module-is-relative-but-outside-this-draw + **0** module-inside-the-draw-and-declares-the-leaf + **3** module-inside-the-draw-but-declares-no-such-name; `unclassified: 0`. THE ONLY CLASS THAT IS THE LANE'S OPEN WORK IS CLASS 7, AND IT IS EMPTY, which is a correction of this instrument's own first answer rather than a happy accident: the first version filed 788 rows there by asking only whether the binding's module was relative and never whether the draw CONTAINED that module — every sampled example was a module outside the sample (`utils.js`, `compiler/state.js`), and the boundary check alone moved the class to 533; the last 3 rows were `import * as acorn from '../acorn.js'` read as `acorn` and `import entities from './entities.js'` read as `entities`, where both modules ARE in the draw (ranks 50 and 63 of the admitted list, size-capped) and NEITHER declares a symbol of that name (`acorn.js` declares `parse`, `remove_parens`, …; `entities.js` has exactly `export default {...}`). A BINDING IS NOT A DECLARATION: the edge names a module, its route is the `imports` edge the store already carries (`acorn:*`), and attaching the `uses` row to a namesake would invent a target — that population is class 8, and the member READ of the same namespace resolves where a member exists, measured: `acorn.parse(...)` in `1-parse/read/script.js` lands attached on `…/1-parse/acorn.js:parse:26`. CLASS 4 IS SUB-CLASSIFIED because `no binding for the leaf` is a population and not a verdict: **3,101** engine standard-library names (no project file declares them) + **0** names the draw DOES declare (so no name-keyed lookup could have taken any of the 10,464) + **3,014** chain segments of a name the draw declares nowhere + **4,349** bare reads of names the draw declares nowhere; sub-class sum printed against the class, `unclassified: 0`. THE TWO TABLES CLOSE ON EACH OTHER AND THE CLOSURE IS PRINTED, not claimed: class 1 defers its rows to the OUTGOING table, so the instrument counts rows with BOTH ends unattributed independently of the reason loop and prints the two numbers with an explicit agreement verdict — 1,557 and 1,557, `nothing escapes both`. The outgoing half is exhaustive on the same terms: all 2,900 NULL-source rows = 2,711 file-level (the store's M60/#910 branch rewrote the sentinel; the un-rewritten count is 0) + 189 name-spelled, of which 178 are neither (an external surface or an unpublishable local binding) and 11 whose name the sample declares SOMEWHERE ELSE — reported at the time as a source-side attachment the name pass did not make, and CORRECTED by JSD48 (a name COLLISION with a local binding: both same-file sub-classes read 0). REPRODUCIBILITY WAS STATED AS A BOUND, AND JSD50 RETRACTED IT: the instrument indexes through `indexProjectParallel`, and three consecutive runs on the same tree read 14,343 / 14,335 / 14,336 detached rows and 1,564 / 1,556 / 1,557 in class 1 — a ~10-row (0.07%) spread with `unclassified: 0` in every run and no class ever emptying or changing sign. That spread was the STORE's, not the instrument's noise: with the settlement pass live the same instrument on the same draw reads 14,324 detached (class 1 at 1,545) against 14,338 (1,559) with the pass neutralised and nothing else changed, and the fixed point makes the total a function of the draw. Records: `store-resolution-jsd50.before.json` / `.after.json`.
decisions.decision: MEASURED 2026-10-11 in `script/m14/javascript-store-resolution.mts`: the reason codes for the outgoing defect half and the eight detached classes are computed in one pass over `brain_relationship`, printed as a table that includes the classes this draw has NONE of (a class absent because it matched nothing and a class absent because the code stopped emitting it look identical in a table that only prints what it saw), and written into the `--json` artifact as `nameSpelledByReason`, `detachedByReason`, `noBindingSubClasses` and `noBindingByShape` so a follow-up can re-take them without re-deriving the conditions. NOT BUILT, and this is the deliberate part: the receiver-typing route that sub-class (c) sizes (3,014 chain segments) would need the analyzer to PUBLISH the members its property reads name — an ontology change with its own wave, gates and oracle co-move, not a resolver tuning; and class 8 is refused BY DESIGN because attaching an import binding to a namesake would put an edge on a symbol that does not exist. ONE GAP FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS ROUND AND NOT SILENTLY INHERITED: `typecheck:scripts` compiles `script/m14/**/*.ts`, a glob that does NOT match `.mts`, so ALL 75 `.mts` instruments in that directory — this one included — sat outside the lane's typecheck. Both of this lane's `.mts` instruments were type-checked under an explicit include and read 0 errors; widening the shared glob is left alone because the same include reads 97 errors across 24 other lanes' `.mts` scripts, so flipping it would turn a passing check red for work that is not this lane's. The gap is reported with its size instead.

decisions.node_type: the OUTGOING residue — a NULL-source row whose source name some file in the project declares
decisions.question: JSD47 counted 11 rows whose source names a name the sample declares and left them as a source-side attachment the name pass did not make. Is that a resolver gap — the last item on the outgoing side — or a class the count could not distinguish?
decisions.resolution: RULED — NOT A GAP, and the count could not have said so: the class asked whether the SAMPLE declares the name and never asked WHICH FILE does. The question that decides a row is whether the row's OWN file declares the name, and for a NULL-source row the row's file is in no join — it is in the ID, which the M14/JS file-level wave made carry `file:<relativePath>` as the anchor of exactly those rows whose source did not resolve. Recovered by longest-prefix match against the sample's own path set (the target that follows the path may itself contain colons, so a split on `:` truncates the path), the class splits three ways. Declared in the row's OWN file IN THE STORE — the miss, same-file evidence the resolver had and did not use: MEASURED **0**. Declared in the row's OWN file in the ANALYZER's output only — a store-path drop rather than a resolver miss: MEASURED **0**. Declared only in OTHER files of the sample — a name COLLISION: MEASURED **11**. Both same-file classes are empty, so the outgoing side has no resolver work, and the 11 are NAMEABLE: six rows in `benchmarking/compare/generate-report.js` (lines 38-39) whose actor is the local `const write = (str) => {…}` declared at line 37, and five in `packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/utils.js` (lines 375-378) whose actor is the local `const RegularElement = (node, { stop }) => {…}` declared at line 374 inside `check_nodes_for_namespace`. Neither file declares a symbol of that name in the STORE or in the ANALYZER's output — both membership tests read false and are printed per row — while `write` is declared once in the draw (`benchmarking/benchmarks/ssr/wrapper/wrapper_bench.js`) and `RegularElement` in six other files, so the only candidate the name pass could reach sits in a file with nothing to do with the row, and attaching these rows would be exactly the wrong-file lie this lane's passes refuse. The 11 are therefore the SAME population as the 178 `neither` rows (an actor that is a local binding the language does not publish); the collision is the only thing that made them read as a different class. MEASURED on the closed 250-file draw, one run of `script/m14/javascript-store-resolution.mts --files=250`: 2,900 NULL-source rows = 2,711 file-level (the store's M60/#910 branch rewrote the sentinel; the un-rewritten count is 0) + 189 name-spelled; the name-spelled half by reason = 0 keyword + **0 own-file/STORE** + **0 own-file/ANALYZER-only** + **11 other-files** + 0 standard-library + 178 neither; sum 189 against the total, `unclassified: 0`, with all six classes printed in a FIXED ORDER INCLUDING THE ZEROS (a class absent from a table reads as none-found whether it means that or no-longer-computed). The totals reproduce the JSD47 run exactly (178 + 11 = 189, 2,711 + 189 = 2,900), so this is a refinement of one class and not a population move.
decisions.decision: MEASURED 2026-10-11 in `script/m14/javascript-store-resolution.mts`: the outgoing reason table's single declared class splits into three by the row's own file, recovered by a longest-prefix match of the id's `file:` anchor against the sample path set; every sub-class is printed in a fixed order with its zero, and the itemized rows travel in the `--json` artifact as `nameSpelledDeclaredRows` (class, own file, and the two membership booleans) so the two zeros can be re-taken rather than re-argued. NO PRODUCT CHANGE, and none owed on this evidence: the resolver is not the actor here; the analyzer attributes a local binding's body to that binding's own name BY DESIGN (the nearest named scope is the most precise actor available, and publishing locals is refused repo-wide — `SymbolKind` has no member for it); and a name-keyed attachment across files is refused by the same contract that makes the name pass refuse ambiguity. What this DOES change is a claim: with both same-file classes at 0, the outgoing side's declared residue stops being carried as open work, and the reason table can no longer hide a miss inside a collision. THE RULE MOVED INTO ONE MODULE AND THE ZEROS BECAME ASSERTIONS in the same round: `script/m14/js-ontology/js-source-classification.ts` holds the classification, the row-id anchor recovery and the engine-enumerated standard-library surface (pasted into two instruments before this round, and the store instrument plus `js-detached-triage.mts` now import it instead), because a rule written twice is a rule that drifts (the JSD44 lesson, where correcting one of four copies left three refusing the names it had just admitted); and `script/m14/verify-js-source-attribution.ts` builds a fixture whose answer is known before the run — a file declaring `caller` with a call inside it, a local `const write = (text) => {…}` in a file that declares no `write`, and `lib/stranger.js`, which does — then classifies every row through the real indexer: 12 checks, 12 pass, exit 0. FALSIFIED IN TWO ARMS, each restored byte-identically by sha256: with the store's insert-time same-file source lookup neutralised the gate reads 10 of 12, failing exactly B4 (own-store) and B9 (the control) with the collision checks unaffected (sha256 `d60d633f1f14305afa38bd5925246297c4fc009cf96a29d448de718e52b1ab84` before and after); with the row-id anchor recovery broken it reads 8 of 12, failing A1, B2, B3 and B7 (sha256 `52fdd17007094d83b096a5c1e3540397bb129c0f58a21a026d6a7939b9911d2d`). THE CLASS'S LABEL WAS CORRECTED WITH IT: it read `the resolver had same-file evidence and did not use it`, but the store DOES look at insert time (`nameToSymbol.get(sourceName) ?? nameToSymbol.get(sourceLeaf)`) while the class is computed from `brain_symbol` read back after the run — so a non-zero reading means the insert-time and read-back symbol sets DISAGREE about the row's own file rather than that a lookup was skipped, and the printed label now says that. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY WRITING THE GATE, both recorded because they are what the checks are for: its summary line was typed (twelve checks under a hardcoded `10 of 10`, the same shape the binding gate shipped earlier in this milestone with `32 of 32` against 33) and a module verdict dropped the row's own file on the file-level class (the instrument never needed it; B7 does).

decisions.node_type: STORE DETERMINISM — the same source indexed twice must resolve every edge to the same target
decisions.question: The store instrument reproduces to a bound: four runs of the same 250-file draw read 14,343 / 14,335 / 14,336 / 14,339 detached rows with 1,564 / 1,556 / 1,557 / 1,560 in class 1, and this doc attributed the spread to class 1 — “the population whose SOURCE resolution is a race between workers”. Is that the mechanism, and how large is the divergence it leaves in the graph a consumer queries?
decisions.resolution: RULED — and the earlier attribution was WRONG, which is the finding: class 1 is a SOURCE-side population and the spread this doc bounded does NOT sit there. `script/m14/verify-resolution-determinism.ts` indexes the same deterministic 250-file draw into TWO separate projects and compares every `brain_relationship` row by its endpoints.
